turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Meera, this dressing is sticking a bit, I'll ease it off. Tell me if it pulls.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Slowly please, I am very scared already. Is it looking bad?

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): The gauze has quite a yellow stain, and the skin around the stitch line is red. I'll leave it open for the doctor. Temperature now is 37.9, pulse 96, BP 118/74, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): 37.9 is fever, no? Last night at home it was hundred and one... no, hundred and two Fahrenheit. I got such a fright.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was warm near eleven, fan was off. The pad I changed yesterday was wet also.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm Dr Iyer. Meera, when was the caesarean done?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Twelve days... no, ten days back, at the nursing home. Lower segment, a routine one, they said. I have been anxious since I came home.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ten days on, and this visit is for the wound.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The stitch place is red, there is dirty pus-like discharge, and I had fever in the night. Will it open up? Do I need another operation? Kindly tell me straight.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll answer after I've looked, guessing won't help you. When did the redness start?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Since two days, I think...
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Not two days. I saw the red edge four days back, at the sponge bath. She is mixing the days.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I cannot place it, Sunday or after, two or four. With dates I will say last winter or the one before and still be wrong. The oozing, when that began, I cannot say either.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): So redness between two and four days, and the discharge you cannot date. Any fever before last night?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Only last night I am sure of. I took Crocin, six hundred and fifty I thought... no, the strip says five hundred milligrams, two tablets. Is 102 dangerous?
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): 102 Fahrenheit overnight is a real fever, 37.9 now is still mildly raised, not an emergency by itself. Is the wound painful?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Little little pain, worse when I get up or turn over. I started to say when the baby kicks, but he is outside only, sorry. Does pain mean the stitch is giving way?
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The pain is from day one. Redness is the new part. She feeds the baby, so she stays tired.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tiredness too. Any chills or shivering with the fever?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No chills. I was just cold from the fan.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was shivering near midnight. She said her teeth were almost chattering, then told me to leave it.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): That was the fan, Shanti, not real chills. Doctor, which one of us will you believe?
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll record that the two of you don't agree on chills. Any vomiting?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. Motions are normal, and urine has no burning.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): What medicines have you used since the operation?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): The antibiotic, white and yellow capsules, Augmentin...
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, 625, it is on the chemist cover.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, 625, I nearly said six hundred. Twice a day. The course was five days... or was it seven? I think two tablets were still in the foil.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Discharge summary said seven days. She stopped short. I saw those two tablets day before yesterday.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Augmentin 625 twice a day, written for seven days, maybe not completed. Taking it now?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Not now, and I can't tell you the day I stopped. I also take the red iron tablets, one in the morning, and Crocin when there is pain. Will iron worsen the infection?
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): No, iron won't feed it, continue one every morning. Calcium, or any acidity tablet?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): The big white calcium tablet, once a day, yes. Pantoprazole I stopped after four days, acidity went. Is calcium fine with a new antibiotic?
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep the calcium once daily. Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. No allergies.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Day two after the operation she got a rash after the painkiller injection. The nurse there said maybe that painkiller. She has kept off it since.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): It was heat rash from the blanket, I don't accept an allergy. I don't remember the painkiller's name. Can I still take pain tablets, and does the baby get them in the milk?
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll steer clear of that painkiller, the story is muddy. The antibiotic I choose is generally alright in breastfeeding. Let me look at the wound first.

[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Redness about three centimetres either side of the lower cut, tender, yellow discharge in the middle. Edges are not black. The abdomen is soft, and there is no collection under the skin.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No collection, so no second operation? Say it once more, please. Can this go into the blood? Are you admitting me?

[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a superficial wound infection, no operation and no admission today. I can't fully exclude a deeper infection until we see how you settle, but today's exam doesn't show one.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): What tests? Will a swab hurt much? I know I am asking too much.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): A wound swab, a blood count, and a CRP. The swab is just a soft tip in the discharge. Nurse, please take it when we're done talking.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): And the antibiotic gets changed, yes? Five or seven days, I honestly still don't know.

[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll change it. Cefuroxime 500 mg by mouth, twice a day, for five days, after you collect it from the pharmacy downstairs. Crocin 500 for pain or fever, up to three times a day, plus the iron and calcium as now.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Is cefuroxime safe while I feed? If the baby gets loose motion? Do I cover the wound? My neighbour said to put turmeric.

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Cefuroxime is acceptable in breastfeeding. Stop and phone if the baby gets loose stools or a rash. No turmeric, no oil, no powder on it. Leave the wound open, or use a loose clean gauze, and wash your hands first.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back in two days, better or not, so I can recheck. If the redness spreads quickly, or the fever climbs past last night, or you feel faint, come the same day.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the swab result be phoned, or only when I come? They said my sugar in pregnancy was normal. That is not causing this, no?

[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll talk through the report when you come, unless a result needs a faster antibiotic change, then the clinic will phone. A normal pregnancy sugar doesn't change this plan.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me give it back. Ten days after the caesarean, redness for about two to four days, discharge you cannot date, fever of 102 Fahrenheit last night and 37.9 here.

[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Augmentin 625 twice daily was written for seven days and may not have been finished. No vomiting, and you two disagree on the chills. A painkiller rash that you don't call an allergy, then swab, blood count, CRP, cefuroxime, and review in two days.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is right, thank you. Shanti, we go to the pharmacy first, I will ask you if the new name slips.
[SEG0054] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take the swab now, Meera. Sit forward a little, then you can settle your saree.

spec.situation: Patient 10 days after a hernia, appendix or caesarean operation; wound redness and discharge, fever the night before; nurse removes dressing and describes it; patient is vague about antibiotic course ('five days... or was it seven'); wound swab and antibiotic change.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
